units.text: INT. ABANDONED CAROUSEL WORKSHOP - NIGHT
A cavernous shed of peeling paint and sawdust.
Dozens of wooden horses hang from the rafters on chains, their glass eyes catching the light of a camping lantern.
Half-carved zebras lie on workbenches.
A pipe organ sits dead under a tarp.
TEODORA VANCE-MBEKI (30s, parka, flashlight clipped to her collar) pushes through the door, brushes cobwebs off her hair, and stops under the hanging horses.
DESMOND CHALK (40s, real-estate blazer, laminated clipboard) follows her in, sneezing.
Near the back, a gaunt man in a leather apron stands motionless at the workbench with his back to them: OLD HARLAN (70s, hands like roots).
As you can see, the property has character.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: It has dust.
units.name: TEODORA

units.text: Dust is character that has been left alone.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Old Harlan does not turn.
Teodora raises her flashlight.
The beam finds his shoulder, and then the bench in front of him, where a small wooden horse sits with its mane half-painted in red.
Excuse me, sir? We didn't know anyone was in here.
units.name: TEODORA

units.text: He lifts the brush.
Dips it.
Draws a single, slow line down the horse's neck.
Desmond steps closer, reading his clipboard as he goes, and trips on a coil of rope.
He grabs a hanging horse to steady himself and the chain groans.
Teodora catches the clipboard as it flies, and Harlan lays the brush down without a sound.
He wasn't on the listing.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Neither was the smell.
units.name: TEODORA

units.text: Old Harlan turns.
His face is smooth, painted, a carved face with a hinge at the jaw.
It opens.
Closing time.
units.name: OLD HARLAN

units.text: Overhead, every horse begins, very slowly, to turn.
